The rifle was included in her arsenal at the insistence of Jango Fett,<ref name="AotCVD" /> and she stored it in a mandible of her airspeeder.<ref name="AotCIC" /> It was a versatile weapon that she modified with an [[Optical/Thermal-imaging scope]] which provided for extreme accuracy, [[power amplifier circuitry]] which increased the fire rate and a [[recoil-damping stock]] to lessen the effect of the increased power.<ref name="FF73">{{FactFile|73|WES 3-4|Zam Wesell's Weapons}}</ref> The rifle would eventually be used to destroy her assassin droid, ASN-121, during the plot to assassinate Senator Amidala.<ref name="SW:E2" />

Due to her experience, Wesell also carried a universal key and explosives to use as part of her arsenal. She kept explosives as part of her arsenal during the Infant of Shaa incident, when she was attacked by a giant Seylott beast. During the encounter, she employed these devices to kill the creature.<ref name="SW:JF" /> Wesell also created her own explosive polymer, which she put to use while escaping a cell on Kuat during the hunt for Hurlo Holowan. The explosives were able to be concealed while the authorities took her blaster and universal key.<ref name="SWAN5" />

===Assassin droid===
{{Main|ASN-121/Legends}}
{{Quote|Senator Jubben. STATUS: Terminated. Baron Wazado. STATUS: Terminated. Senator Amidala. STATUS: ABORTABORTABORTABOR-|An excerpt from the recovered log of Zam Wesell's ASN-121|<ref name="NEGD" />}}
[[File:Assasssindroid.jpg|thumb|left|150px|ASN-121 assassin droid]]
Zam Wesell's personal assassin droid was a custom-made creation by the [[Malkite Poisoners]] upon her request. To hide its true origins, the Malkite Poisoners created the automaton from commonplace parts. The droid was equipped with a wide array of features, including unprecedented environmental awareness and stealth abilities.<ref name="NEGD" /> It also possessed an [[Photoreceptor/Legends|infrared photoreceptor]],<ref name="FF43" /> an eavesdropping recorder, a tangle net, and a stinger blaster. These tools were specifically installed for use on stealth missions.<ref name="NEGD" /> Furthermore, the droid's narrow shape minimized the profile for pursuers or those attacking from ahead, creating a smaller target.<ref name="AotCIC" />

The droid was constructed with a powerful repulsorlift engine<ref name="DB-ASN">{{DB|droid|asn121|ASN-121}}</ref> which was rated military-plus. Powered by fusion generator, the repulsorlift allowed the droid to reach near-orbit altitudes.<ref name="NEGD" /> Because it was independently powered, the repulsorlift ensured good balance for the droid, even under unusual loads.<ref name="AotCIC" /> The automaton also had the ability to reroute its electric current to its metal posterior, shocking stowaways or any item which would interfere with it.<ref name="NEGD" />

Wesell had the ability to equip the droid with a variety of implements and weapons, such as a harpoon gun, sniper blaster, gas dispenser, spy sensors, flamethrower, durasteel drills and cutters.<ref name="NEGD" /><ref name="AotCIC" /><ref name="DB-ASN" /> All of these were easily installed into the central tool socket, which was designed to accommodate these items. The central socket also had the ability to hold canisters, which could have been filled with toxic biological agents or explosives.<ref name="NEGD" />

During the second attempt on the life of Senator Amidala, Wesell loaded the ASN-121 assassin droid with a canister of kouhuns. She also disabled the ability to redirect its electrical current, hoping to minimize its electric signature. After using its tools to dispatch the creatures, the droid was forced into a retreat when it was spotted by Obi-Wan Kenobi. Kenobi jumped through the apartment window and grasped the droid. Kenobi's weight of 63&#32;kg neither deterred nor slowed the droid.<ref name="NEGD" /> The droid, however, was able to shock Kenobi using its electro-defense grid as he rode it through the skylanes of Coruscant. ASN-121 also attempted to remove the clinging Jedi by brushing up against a skyscraper.<ref name="SW:E2-C1">[[Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones (comic series)|''Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones'' comic adaptation]]: [[Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones 1|Issue 1]]</ref> In an attempt to kill the Jedi, Wesell used her sniper rifle and shot the droid, causing Kenobi to plummet toward the planet surface.<ref name="SW:E2" /><ref name="SW:CL" /> The wreckage of the droid was later salvaged and a status log of Wesell's bounties was recovered at that time.<ref name="NEGD" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Character development and portrayal===
{{Quote|The costume and weaponry really help make the character. You look at yourself in the mirror, and you say, {{'}}''This'' is how I'm going to be.' |[[Leeanna Walsman]], on portraying Zam Wesell|<ref name="Magazine UK 37">[[Star Wars: The Official Magazine 37|''Star Wars: The Official Magazine'' 37]]</ref>}}
[[File:ZamWesellMabariArmorSkirt-ImageAttack.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The creation of Wesell's [[Armorweave/Legends|Mabari armorweave]] skirt by costumers]]
The character of Zam Wesell was played by actress [[Leeanna Walsman]] in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="SW:E2" /> Walsman also provided the voice for the same character in the game ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''.<ref name="SW:BH" /> However, Wesell was voiced by [[Diane Michelle]] in the ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' expansion pack [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|''Clone Campaigns'']].<ref name="SW:GB-Expansion">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref>

Wesell was originally created as an antagonist in ''Attack of the Clones''. Early drafts of the ''Episode II'' scripts referred to Wesell as a "C.A.T.," a [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] Trooper, instead of "Zam Wesell."<ref name="DB" /> Her first appearance in [[canon]], however, was in the one-shot comic [[Star Wars: Jango Fett (one-shot)|''Star Wars: Jango Fett'']] which predated the film by two months.<ref name="SW:E2" /><ref name="SW:JF" /> Wesell was not originally conceived as a changeling or shapeshifting being. Rather, this concept developed well after principal photography for ''Attack of the Clones'' had begun. As a result, Walsman was originally unaware of Wesell's species type. The transformations and alien appearance were created digitally by superimposing a "mask" over Walsman's face.<ref name="DB-C" /> Wesell, as a changeling, was then included in the one-shot ''Star Wars: Jango Fett'' and in the [[Star Wars Gamer 10|tenth issue]] of [[Star Wars Gamer]].<ref name="SW:JF" /><ref name="SWG10">[[Star Wars Gamer 10|''Star Wars Gamer'' 10]]</ref>

Details and background information for Zam Wesell were created with the one-shot comics ''Star Wars: Jango Fett'', ''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]'', and the game ''Star Wars: Bounty Hunter''.<ref name="SW:ZW" /><ref name="SW:BH" /><ref name="SW:JF" /> Subsequent appearances in ''[[Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive]]'' and ''[[The Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'' further expanded her role in the life of Boba Fett and provided more details about the plot to assassinate Senator Padmé Amidala.<ref name="Obi-Wan" /><ref name="BF1" /> Wesell was drawn upon heavily in the creation of the backstory for Theomet Danlé and the first failed attempt on Senator Amidala by the user "[[winstonvalleyjedi]]" in the [[StarWars.com|online]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|''Hyperspace'']] feature ''[[What's The Story?]]''<ref name="DB-TD" /> Additionally, while Wesell did not appear in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'',<ref name="LEGO1">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]''</ref> she made a non-canonical appearance in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''.<ref name="LEGO2">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref>

The inspiration for Zam's timid old-man persona "Marby Welcus" appears to have been "Marcus Welby" of the popular longplaying television series of the 1970s, [[Wikipedia:Marcus Welby, M.D.|''Marcus Welby, M.D.'']]

===Continuity issues===
====''Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones''====
In the scenes where Zam Wesell is talking to Jango Fett and when she loads the kouhuns in the droid ASN-121 from ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' Zam can be seen sporting a [[WESTAR-34 blaster pistol]] in her holster instead of the usual KYD-21 she uses in later scenes and keeps in the same holster.<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref> The first two scenes (with the WESTAR) were done during [[Wikipedia:Pick-up (filmmaking)|pick-ups]] shooting in [[March]] [[2001]] in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]], while the others scenes were from [[Wikipedia:Principal photography|principal photography]] in [[July]] [[2000]] in [[Wikipedia:Australia|Australia]]. [[Pablo Hidalgo]] hypothesized that the [[Wikipedia:Prop|prop]] of the KDY might have not been sent to the United Kingdom for the pick-ups.<ref name="Blusky">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3mmkkoqklf22k|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2026-05-24|archivedate=20260524161354}}</ref>

====''The New Essential Guide to Characters''====
Unlike other sources, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' lists much of Wesell's vital information as "unknown." This, however, does not pose direct conflicts with other established sources, but the ''Guide'' directly offers the possibility that much of Wesell's backstory may have been prefabricated in-universe by the character as a web of carefully concocted lies.<ref name="NEGTC" /> For example, Wesell's gender is listed as "unknown" in the ''Guide'', but is confirmed as female in sources such as the Databank.<ref name="DB" /> Furthermore, while all sources call the character "Zam Wesell," the ''Guide'' states that it may not be her real name.<ref name="NEGTC" />

====''The Official Star Wars Fact Files''====
A minor inconsistency arises between the ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]s'' and the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''Star Wars: Bounty Hunter''. The video game takes place in 32 BBY, five years before the crossing of contracts between Dreddon the Hutt and Vigo Antonin. Yet, Fact Files [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 53|53]], [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 65|65]], and [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 71|71]] state that Wesell's first encounter with Jango Fett was at Dreddon's palace.<ref name="SW:BH" /><ref name="FF53" /><ref name="FF65" /><ref name="FF71" />

Another continuity issue arises in Fact File [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 101|101]], which states that Wesell, in preparation for the first assassination attempt on Senator Amidala, planted an explosive device on the landing platform where the senator was expected to land. Wesell then staked out over a kilometer away and detonated the bomb when she saw Amidala's decoy, believing it was Amidala herself, step out of the vessel and onto the platform.<ref name="FF101" /> This conflicts with Wesell's Databank entry, which states that Wesell posed as a reporter and conned a drunk Theomet Danlé into planting the explosive on the ship. Whether or not Wesell staked out the landing pad in this situation is not stated, but the Databank cites the explosion as having come from the bomb planted inside the vessel.<ref name="DB-TD" />

===Non-canon and ambiguously canon appearances===
[[File:Zam_Wesell_Lego.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Advertising image featuring Zam Wesell's model for ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'']]
The [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO]] model for Wesell does not appear in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game'', as the model was unused.<ref name="LEGO1" /> However, the character and the attempt to assassinate Padmé Amidala both make non-canonical appearances in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga''. The game also includes the speeder chase between Wesell and the Jedi Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi.<ref name="LEGO2" /> Wesell has an appearance in the [[Wizards of the Coast]] scenario ''Two Jedi Walk Into a Bar''. In this [[Roleplaying game|role-playing]] scenario, the player revisits the Outlander Club following the speeder chase in 22 BBY and creates a what-if situation in which Jango Fett wanted to keep Wesell alive and help her escape the Jedi rather than meet her ultimate canonical fate.<ref name="WotC-TwoJedi">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=swminis/article/twojedi|text=Two Jedi Walk Into a Bar|int=Two Jedi Walk Into a Bar}}</ref>
